import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.55

by V. P. Shunkov

A group $G$ of the form $G = F \leftthreetimes H$ (a semidirect product of a normal
subgroup $F$ by a subgroup $H$) is said to be a *Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and
complement $H$* if $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$ and
$F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$.
Do there exist Frobenius $p$-groups?

Here a $p$-group is a group in which every element has order a power of the prime $p$.
A finite Frobenius group has kernel and complement of coprime orders, so a Frobenius
$p$-group is necessarily infinite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«6.55»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/--
A group $G$ is a *Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$* if
$G = F \leftthreetimes H$, i.e. $F$ is a normal subgroup and $H$ is a subgroup with
$F \cap H = 1$ and $FH = G$, such that $H \cap H^g = 1$ for every $g \in G \setminus H$ and
$F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$.

Here the conjugate $H^g$ is `MulAut.conj g • H`.
-/
structure IsFrobeniusGroup (F H : Subgroup G) : Prop where
  normal : F.Normal
  isComplement' : F.IsComplement' H
  inf_conj_eq_bot : ∀ g ∉ H, H ⊓ MulAut.conj g • H = ⊥
  kernel_eq : (F : Set G) \ {1} = (⋃ g : G, ((MulAut.conj g • H : Subgroup G) : Set G))ᶜ

/-- The defining conditions are degenerately satisfied by the trivial complement $H = 1$
with kernel $F = G$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFrobeniusGroup_top_bot : IsFrobeniusGroup (⊤ : Subgroup G) ⊥ where
  normal := inferInstance
  isComplement' := Subgroup.isComplement'_top_bot
  inf_conj_eq_bot _ _ := bot_inf_eq _
  kernel_eq := by
    ext x
    simp

/-- The defining conditions are degenerately satisfied by the complement $H = G$
with trivial kernel $F = 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFrobeniusGroup_bot_top : IsFrobeniusGroup (⊥ : Subgroup G) ⊤ where
  normal := inferInstance
  isComplement' := Subgroup.isComplement'_bot_top
  inf_conj_eq_bot g hg := (hg (Subgroup.mem_top g)).elim
  kernel_eq := by
    ext x
    simp

/--
Do there exist Frobenius $p$-groups?

That is, is there a prime $p$ and a group $G$ in which every element has order a power
of $p$, such that $G$ is a Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$ for some
subgroups $F$ and $H$? As usual for Frobenius groups, the complement is required to be
a nontrivial proper subgroup, $1 \ne H \ne G$: the defining conditions are degenerately
satisfied by $H = 1$ (with $F = G$) and by $H = G$ (with $F = 1$).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (F H : Subgroup G),
      p.Prime ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ IsFrobeniusGroup F H ∧ H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.55»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table's reading (existential over a prime p and a group G with all elements of p-power order, Frobenius in the notebook's sense, with the standard nontriviality 1 ≠ H ≠ G) is the only sensible one; I confirmed the degenerate cases H = 1 and H = G do satisfy the literal definition, so the nontriviality condition is indeed required.
modeling_decisions: `p`-group is formalized as `IsPGroup p G` with `p.Prime` (every element has order a power of the prime p); `p` is quantified existentially inside the answer. `p.Prime` is essential: without it e.g. S₃ with p = 6 would make the statement trivially true.

`G = F ⋋ H` is encoded as `F.Normal ∧ F.IsComplement' H` (F ∩ H = 1 and FH = G). Normality of F is redundant given the other conditions (F is determined as a conjugation-invariant set) but is part of 'of the form F ⋋ H', so it is kept.

The conjugate H^g is `MulAut.conj g • H` = gHg⁻¹; since the condition is quantified over all g ∉ H (a set closed under inversion) and the union is over all g ∈ G, the gHg⁻¹ vs g⁻¹Hg convention does not matter.

Nontriviality `H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤` (equivalently F ≠ ⊤ ∧ F ≠ ⊥ under IsComplement') is added in the theorem body, not in the definition, following the decomposition table; the literal definition is degenerately satisfied by (F,H) = (⊤,⊥) and (⊥,⊤), which is proved in two `category test` theorems.
No `Infinite G` hypothesis is added since the source does not state one (it follows from the other hypotheses for nontrivial Frobenius p-groups).
The group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files (1_74, 1_40).

by V. P. Shunkov

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«6.55»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/--
A group $G$ is a *Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$* if
$G = F \leftthreetimes H$ (that is, $F$ is a normal subgroup of $G$ and $H$ is a complement of
$F$, so that $F \cap H = 1$ and $FH = G$), $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$, and
$F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$.

Here $H^g$ denotes the conjugate subgroup `MulAut.conj g • H`. This is the literal definition
from the notebook; it is degenerately satisfied when $H = 1$ (with $F = G$) and when $H = G$
(with $F = 1$).

structure IsFrobeniusGroup (F H : Subgroup G) : Prop where
  /-- The kernel $F$ is normal in $G$. -/

  /-- $H$ is a complement of $F$, so $G = F \leftthreetimes H$. -/
  isComplement' : F.IsComplement' H
  /-- $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$. -/
  inf_conj_eq_bot : ∀ g : G, g ∉ H → H ⊓ MulAut.conj g • H = ⊥
  /-- $F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$. -/
  kernel_sdiff_one_eq :
    (F : Set G) \ {1} = Set.univ \ ⋃ g : G, ((MulAut.conj g • H : Subgroup G) : Set G)

/-- The degenerate case $H = 1$, $F = G$ satisfies the literal definition. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFrobeniusGroup_top_bot : IsFrobeniusGroup (⊤ : Subgroup G) ⊥ where
  normal := inferInstance
  isComplement' := Subgroup.isComplement'_top_bot
  inf_conj_eq_bot _ _ := bot_inf_eq _
  kernel_sdiff_one_eq := by simp

/-- The degenerate case $H = G$, $F = 1$ satisfies the literal definition. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFrobeniusGroup_bot_top : IsFrobeniusGroup (⊥ : Subgroup G) ⊤ where
  normal := inferInstance
  isComplement' := Subgroup.isComplement'_bot_top
  inf_conj_eq_bot g hg := (hg (Subgroup.mem_top g)).elim
  kernel_sdiff_one_eq := by simp [Set.iUnion_const]

/--
Do there exist Frobenius $p$-groups?

That is, is there a prime $p$ and a group $G$ in which every element has order a power of $p$
such that $G$ is a Frobenius group with some kernel $F$ and complement $H$? The complement $H$
is required to be a nontrivial proper subgroup, $1 \ne H \ne G$; this is the standard
nontriviality assumption on Frobenius groups, and without it the question has a trivial
positive answer (see `isFrobeniusGroup_top_bot` and `isFrobeniusGroup_bot_top`).
-/

theorem kourovka.«6.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (F H : Subgroup G),
      p.Prime ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ IsFrobeniusGroup F H ∧ H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤ := by

The single-slot table is correct: the question is an existential yes/no question, p should be existential, and the literal definition needs the standard nontriviality 1 ≠ H ≠ G to avoid a trivial positive answer (both degenerate cases are proved as tests in the file).
modeling_decisions: Conjugate subgroup H^g is modelled as `MulAut.conj g • H` (= gHg⁻¹, verified: x ∈ MulAut.conj g • H ↔ g⁻¹ x g ∈ H). The notebook's H^g is usually g⁻¹Hg, but both the condition 'for all g ∉ H' and the union over all g ∈ G are invariant under g ↦ g⁻¹, so the two conventions give the same predicate.
G = F ⋊ H (internal semidirect product) is modelled as `F.Normal ∧ F.IsComplement' H`, i.e. F normal and (f, h) ↦ f * h bijective, which is exactly F ∩ H = 1 and FH = G.
H ∩ H^g = 1 is stated as `H ⊓ MulAut.conj g • H = ⊥` at the subgroup level; F \ {1} = G \ ⋃ H^g is stated verbatim as an equation of sets in G.

The nontriviality 1 ≠ H ≠ G is placed in the theorem statement (`H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤`) rather than in the definition, so the definition matches the notebook literally and the added assumption is visible; two `category test` lemmas prove that the literal definition is degenerately satisfied by (F,H) = (⊤,⊥) and (⊥,⊤), documenting why the exclusion is necessary. H ≠ ⊤ forces F ≠ ⊥ and H ≠ ⊥ forces F ≠ ⊤ via the complement condition, so no extra condition on F is needed.

'p-group' is read as: p is a prime and every element of G has order a power of p (`p.Prime ∧ IsPGroup p G`), the standard infinite-group meaning; p is quantified existentially, as the notes require. Finiteness is not assumed (a finite Frobenius p-group cannot exist).
The group G is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74, 19_25, 20_76).

  normal : F.Normal
  isComplement' : F.IsComplement' H

  isComplement' := Subgroup.isComplement'_top_bot
  inf_conj_eq_bot _ _ := bot_inf_eq _
  sdiff_one_eq := by

  sdiff_one_eq := by
    simp [Set.iUnion_const]

The nontriviality `H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤` from the decomposition notes is imposed at theorem level and explained in the docstring; two proved `category test` lemmas show the literal definition is degenerately satisfied by (⊤, ⊥) and (⊥, ⊤) in every group, justifying the restriction.

statement_blocks.kourovka.«6.55»:
/--
Do there exist Frobenius $p$-groups? That is, are there a prime $p$ and a $p$-group $G$
(a group in which every element has order a power of $p$) which is a Frobenius group with
some kernel $F$ and complement $H$?

The literal definition is satisfied by the degenerate decompositions $H = 1$, $F = G$ and
$H = G$, $F = 1$ of any group, so, as is standard for Frobenius groups, we require
$1 \ne H \ne G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (F H : Subgroup G),
      p.Prime ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ IsFrobeniusGroupWith F H ∧ H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry
